title: NYC School Survey, 2026
source: NYC Public Schools (DOE), NYC School Survey 2026 public data files (K-12 Teacher, Student and K-12 Family)

teacher_principal_effective.label: Teachers: principal is an effective manager
teacher_principal_effective.definition: Share of responding teachers who agree or strongly agree: "The principal/program leader at this school is an effective manager who makes the school run smoothly." (Teacher survey q29; part of the Teacher-Principal Trust measure.)
teacher_principal_effective.source_field: t_q29_P (row-2 label "Agree/Strongly agree") under "q29. The principal/program leader at this school is an effective manager who makes the school run smoothly."; sheet "Teacher Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_teacher.xlsx

teacher_recommend.label: Teachers who would recommend the school
teacher_recommend.definition: Share of responding teachers who agree or strongly agree: "I would recommend this school to parents/guardians seeking a place for their child." (Teacher survey q22; School Commitment measure.)
teacher_recommend.source_field: t_q22_P (row-2 label "Agree/Strongly agree") under "q22. I would recommend this school to parents/guardians seeking a place for their child."; sheet "Teacher Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_teacher.xlsx

student_safe.label: Students who feel safe in hallways and cafeteria
student_safe.definition: Share of responding students (grades 6-12) answering Safe or Very Safe to "Do you feel safe in the hallways and the cafeteria?" (Student survey q40; Safety measure.)
student_safe.source_field: s_q40_P (row-2 label "Safe/Very Safe") under "q40. Do you feel safe in the hallways and the cafeteria?"; sheet "Student Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_student.xlsx

student_supported.label: Students who feel supported by teachers
student_supported.definition: Share of responding students answering Most or All of their teachers to "How many of your teachers do you feel support you when you are upset?" (Student survey q13; Student-Teacher Trust measure.)
student_supported.source_field: s_q13_P (row-2 label "Most of your teachers/All of your teachers") under "q13. How many of your teachers do you feel support you when you are upset?"; sheet "Student Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_student.xlsx

student_trusted_adult.label: Students with a trusted adult at school
student_trusted_adult.definition: Share of responding students answering Often or Very often to "How often do you feel like there is at least one trusted adult at this school you could talk to if you needed to?" (Student survey q34; Social-Emotional measure.)
student_trusted_adult.source_field: s_q34_P (row-2 label "Often/Very often") under "q34. How often do you feel like there is at least one trusted adult at this school you could talk to if you needed to?"; sheet "Student Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_student.xlsx

student_vaping_often.label: Students who say peers vape often
student_vaping_often.definition: Share of responding students answering Very often or Often to "How often do students in this school vape?" This is the unfavorable side of the item; DOE's percent favorable is the remainder (Sometimes/Never). New in 2026, reported under Additional Questions and not scored in any measure.
student_vaping_often.source_field: s_q59_N (row-2 label "Very often/Often") under "q59. How often do students in this school vape?"; sheet "Student Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_student.xlsx

parent_satisfied.label: Families satisfied with the education
parent_satisfied.definition: Share of responding K-12 families answering Satisfied or Very satisfied to "How satisfied are you with the following? The education my child has received this year." (Family survey q36; Family Satisfaction with Child's Education measure.)
parent_satisfied.source_field: p_q36_P (row-2 label "Satisfied/Very satisfied") under "q36. How satisfied are you with the following? The education my child has received this year."; sheet "Family Pos & Neg %", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_guardian.xlsx

teacher_responses.label: Teacher responses
teacher_responses.definition: Number of completed teacher surveys. Full-time teachers and staff employed at the school on Nov. 1, 2025 were eligible; DOE counts guidance counselors in the teacher population.
teacher_responses.source_field: "Total Teacher Response Counts"; sheet "new total tab", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_teacher.xlsx

teacher_response_rate.label: Teacher response rate
teacher_response_rate.definition: Completed teacher surveys divided by the eligible teacher population. For charter schools DOE estimates the population from enrollment or staffing.
teacher_response_rate.source_field: "Total Teacher Response Rate"; sheet "new total tab", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_teacher.xlsx

student_responses.label: Student responses
student_responses.definition: Number of completed student surveys. Students in grades 6-12 enrolled by Oct. 1, 2025 were eligible; schools without those grades have no student survey.

student_response_rate.label: Student response rate
student_response_rate.definition: Completed student surveys divided by students in grades 6-12 enrolled by Oct. 1, 2025.

parent_responses.label: Family responses
parent_responses.definition: Number of completed K-12 family surveys. Families receive one survey per enrolled child.

parent_response_rate.label: Family response rate
parent_response_rate.definition: Completed family surveys divided by the number of enrolled students (one survey per child, students enrolled by Oct. 1, 2025).

score_teacher_principal_trust.label: Teacher-principal trust (teacher survey)
score_teacher_principal_trust.definition: DOE measure score: the average percent favorable across the teacher items q28-q34 (respected by, trust, confidence in, effective manager, looks out for staff, puts children first, principal and APs work as a unit).
score_teacher_principal_trust.source_field: "Teacher-Principal Trust Score"; sheet "new total tab", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_teacher.xlsx; file value is 0-100, divided by 100 here

score_instructional_leadership.label: Instructional leadership (teacher survey)
score_instructional_leadership.definition: DOE measure score: the average percent favorable across teacher items q63-q70 on the principal and assistant principals setting expectations, tracking progress, giving feedback and planning instruction with teachers.
score_instructional_leadership.source_field: "Instructional Leadership Score"; sheet "new total tab", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_teacher.xlsx; file value is 0-100, divided by 100 here

score_student_safety.label: Safety (student survey)
score_student_safety.definition: DOE measure score: the average percent favorable across student items q39, q40, q41 (feel safe in classes; hallways and cafeteria; locker rooms and bathrooms), q44 (School Safety Agents), q58 (physical fights), q60 (alcohol/drugs) and q61 (gang activity).
score_student_safety.source_field: "Safety Score"; sheet "Total", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_student.xlsx; file value is 0-100, divided by 100 here

score_student_teacher_trust.label: Student-teacher trust (student survey)
score_student_teacher_trust.definition: DOE measure score: the average percent favorable across student items q11, q12, q13, q27 and q28 (how many teachers are open to students' ideas, treat you with respect, support you when upset, treat students of different backgrounds and genders equally).
score_student_teacher_trust.source_field: "Student-Teacher Trust Score"; sheet "Total", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_student.xlsx; file value is 0-100, divided by 100 here

score_family_satisfaction.label: Family satisfaction with education (family survey)
score_family_satisfaction.definition: DOE measure score: the average percent favorable across family items q31, q32, q33, q36 and q37 (progress in reading and math, understanding grade-level work, satisfaction with the education and with the teachers).
score_family_satisfaction.source_field: "Family Satisfaction with Child's Education Score"; sheet "Total", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_guardian.xlsx; file value is 0-100, divided by 100 here

score_parent_principal_trust.label: Parent-principal trust (family survey)
score_parent_principal_trust.definition: DOE measure score: the average percent favorable across family items q5, q10 and q11 (respected by the principal, trust the principal at their word, principal is an effective manager).
score_parent_principal_trust.source_field: "Parent-Principal Trust Score"; sheet "Total", nyc_doe_school_survey_2026_public_data_file_guardian.xlsx; file value is 0-100, divided by 100 here

notes: Three separate DOE workbooks feed this file (teacher, student, K-12 family); file_url is therefore a list, and each field carries its own file_url.

Percent favorable is DOE's own calculation: favorable responses divided by all favorable plus unfavorable responses to that question. 'I don't know', 'N/A' and blank answers are left out of the denominator (2026 Scoring Technical Guide). DOE rounds the shares to two decimals in the file.

Suppression: the files print 'N/A' where a respondent group had fewer than five responses, or where a question did not apply to the school (e.g. elementary-only items). Those cells are null. Suppressed-cell counts in the columns used here: 'N/A' x558. (The guardian Total sheet also has two '#N/A' Excel-error cells, in its Teacher Response Rate column, which is not used here; the script would null them too.)

A null can also mean the school is simply not in that workbook: only schools serving grades 6-12 have a student survey, and a few District 75 schools appear in a Total sheet (response counts and scores) but not in the question-level sheet.
Only the all-respondents school value is used. The workbooks hold no citywide row; demographic breakdowns are on separate sheets and are not used.
The 2026 student survey was substantially rewritten. DOE says student results are a new baseline and should not be compared with earlier years. Teacher and family surveys had only minor revisions.

Who counts as a teacher: DOE includes guidance counselors in the teacher population. Support staff (paraprofessionals, parent coordinators, social workers, etc.) also take a version of the survey, but the workbook does not say whether they are in these counts. Its response counts sum to 65,980, close to the 66,566 teacher respondents DOE's 2026 citywide deck reports excluding support staff, which suggests teachers only. The 2026 wording of the principal item is 'principal/program leader'; earlier years (and THE CITY's 2023 quote) used 'principal/school leader'.
student_vaping_often is stored as the unfavorable share (students saying peers vape very often or often), so lower is better. It is an Additional Question that DOE does not score in any measure.

student_safe uses q40 (hallways and cafeteria). The same survey also asks about feeling safe in classes (q39; 92% favorable citywide per DOE's 2026 deck) and in locker rooms and bathrooms (q41; 84%). DOE's deck puts q40 at 87% citywide.

score_* fields are DOE measure scores from the workbooks' Total sheets: the average of the percent-favorable values of the measure's questions (checked here against the question-level sheets for sample schools). They are survey-only measures, not the School Quality Report framework ratings (Rigorous Instruction, Effective School Leadership, Trust, Supportive Environment, etc.), which are not in these files.

Response rates come from each group's own workbook, as published (DOE rounds them to two decimals). For charter schools DOE estimates the teacher population. Schools with any response rate above 100%: 0.

Checks against THE CITY's Oct. 7, 2026 guide: P.S. 307 (13K307) principal item = 85% (matches); 539 schools with 95%+ of teachers recommending (THE CITY: about 540); 56 schools where half or more of teachers did not agree they would recommend (THE CITY: 56). THE CITY's 87% citywide figure for the principal item could not be reproduced from this file: summing the file's own response counts gives about 86% (55,823 favorable of 65,033 favorable+unfavorable). The difference may be in how Panorama's citywide report aggregates; it is not a school-level value.
2026 results are also on Panorama Education (secure.panoramaed.com/nycdoe), one page per school; this file uses only DOE's bulk Excel releases.
